cleanIntro: The GI-style 1911 strip, in Springfield's own order: recoil parts first, because the bushing is the only thing holding the plug and spring, then the slide stop, then the slide forward off the frame with the whole front end attached.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber checked, slide eased forward
steps.action: Press the magazine catch and take the magazine out first, then draw the slide back and look into the chamber before letting it run forward again. A 1911 will fire with the magazine out if a round is chambered, so the magazine coming out proves nothing on its own.
steps.aside: Pull slide backwards and check that no cartridge is in the chamber.
steps.quote: Press magazine catch and remove magazine.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 1 (printed p.27, per Figure 27-1 on the page)

steps.title: Eye protection on — a plug and spring are about to be loose
steps.action: Put glasses on before the recoil spring plug moves. That plug is held only by the barrel bushing and it is under the full recoil spring; it is the single most common thing to lose across a room during a 1911 strip.
steps.quote: Before performing any cleaning or maintenance, make sure the firearm is completely unloaded (this includes the magazine and chamber). Wear eye protection.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 1 (printed p.27, per Figure 27-1 on the page)

steps.title: Two-piece guide rod first, if your pistol has one
steps.action: Some full-size Springfields carry a two-piece full-length guide rod instead of the GI-style short guide; on those the front half unscrews with a 5/32 Allen wrench before anything else happens. If a hex socket shows in the front of the frame under the barrel, that is what you have.
steps.quote: If your pistol contains a 2 piece full length guide rod, use a 5/32 Allen wrench to remove the front portion of guide rod.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 1 (printed p.27, per Figure 27-1 on the page)

steps.title: Thumb on the plug, slide back half an inch, bushing clockwise
steps.action: Rest the butt on your knee, grip the slide behind the front sight and move it back about half an inch, then press the recoil spring plug in with your thumb and rotate the barrel bushing clockwise. Keep the muzzle pointed away from your face throughout — the plug is what leaves at speed if the bushing goes past it.
steps.aside: Point muzzle away from face and rotate barrel bushing clockwise.
steps.quote: Move slide rearward, approximately 1/2 inch, grasp firmly to hold in place, and depress recoil spring plug with thumb.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 2 (printed p.27, per Figures 27-2 and 27-3)

steps.title: Never let the bushing off the plug without holding both
steps.action: The bushing is the only thing capturing the plug and spring. Keep your thumb on the plug while the bushing turns, then let plug and spring come forward under control. This is the step that costs people a plug and, occasionally, an eye.
steps.aside: WARNING: Point muzzle away from face to prevent injury in the event plug is ejected by spring.
steps.quote: Do not rotate bushing off of plug unless you have control of plug and spring.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 2 (printed p.27, per Figures 27-2 and 27-3)

steps.title: Plug and spring forward, gently
steps.action: Ease the plug and recoil spring forward off the front of the slide rather than letting go of them. Nothing here should snap.
steps.quote: Cautiously allow plug and recoil spring to move forward
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 3 (printed p.27)

steps.title: Disassembly notch lined up, slide stop out to the left
steps.action: Move the slide back until its disassembly notch — the small semicircular cut, not the slide-stop notch further back — sits over the slide stop, then push the slide stop's shaft from the right side of the frame and draw it out to the left. If it fights you, the notch is not aligned; do not lever it, or you will scar the frame.
steps.aside: Press slide stop shaft on right side of frame and remove slide stop by pulling it out of left side of frame.
steps.quote: Align disassembly notch on slide with slide stop.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 4 (printed p.28, per Figure 28-1)

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame — it takes the whole front end with it
steps.action: Run the slide forward off its rails and off the front of the frame. The barrel, bushing, plug, spring and guide all come with it as an assembly, which is why the recoil parts came out first.
steps.quote: Pull slide forward in its guides and remove slide. Barrel, barrel bushing, recoil spring plug, recoil spring and guide will come with it.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Steps 5-6 (printed p.28, per Figure 28-2)

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide out the back of the slide
steps.action: Take the recoil spring and its guide out through the rear of the slide. Keep them together and note which way the guide sits; it goes back the same way, aligned with the barrel.
steps.quote: Remove recoil spring and guide through back side.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Steps 5-6 (printed p.28, per Figure 28-2)

steps.title: Bushing out the front, then the barrel — strip complete
steps.action: Rotate the barrel bushing the other way — to the left of the slide — and take it out through the front, then tilt the barrel link forward and slide the barrel out of the front of the slide. That is the field strip: frame, slide, barrel, bushing, plug, spring and guide.
steps.aside: Tilt barrel link forward and remove barrel from front of slide
steps.quote: Rotate barrel bushing to left of slide and remove it through the front.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY OF FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 7 (printed p.29, per Figure 29-1)

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, and never reverse a brush mid-bore
steps.action: Push the rod in from the chamber end where you can and run it all the way out at the muzzle. Do not reverse direction with a brush or patch still in the bore — that is how a brush jams and a rod bends.
steps.aside: Do not “reverse” rod direction when patch or brush is in barrel, it might bind.
steps.quote: When possible, insert cleaning rod from chamber end of bore and push rod all the way through so it emerges from muzzle.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — CARE & CLEANING (PDF p.59; this edition prints no page folios)

steps.title: Solvent, then a brush, then dry patches until they come out clean
steps.action: Run a solvent-wet patch through several times, follow with a solvent-wetted bristle brush end to end, then dry patches until they come out clean. Fouling in the bore costs accuracy; fouling in the chamber costs feeding, and the chamber is the part people skip.
steps.aside: Bore fouling can contribute to reduced accuracy, and grease accumulation in the chamber can interfere with proper feeding of cartridges from magazine.
steps.quote: Attach solvent-wetted bristle brush to rod and run back and forth full length of bore as needed until clean of grease and dirt.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — CLEANING PISTOL (PDF p.60-61)

steps.title: A very small amount of oil — stainless takes slightly more
steps.action: Wipe everything down and oil sparingly: enough to protect, not enough to collect grit. Springfield's own note is that stainless pistols want slightly more than blued or parkerized ones, and that surplus oil attracts the dust that jams guns.
steps.aside: Stainless Steel pistols require slightly more lubrication than parkerized or blued pistols.
steps.quote: Only a very small amount of oil is needed to adequately lubricate moving parts and prevent rust.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — CARE & CLEANING (PDF p.59; this edition prints no page folios)

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out — point the back of the slide away from you
deepSteps.action: With the slide off, press the firing pin forward with a pin punch while pushing its tail past the firing pin stop, then draw the stop downward out of the slide. Keep the rear of the slide pointed away from your face as the stop clears: the firing pin spring is compressed behind it.
deepSteps.aside: Remove firing pin and its spring.
deepSteps.quote: If necessary, remove firing pin by pressing it with pin punch while simultaneously pushing firing pin tail past the firing pin stop, then pull firing pin stop downward from slide.
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — PERIODIC CLEANING: EXTRACTOR (printed p.61, per Figure 61-1 on the page)

deepSteps.title: Extractor out through the firing pin stop channel
deepSteps.action: With the stop out, hook the extractor by the groove the firing pin stop runs in and pull it straight back out of the slide. Clean the extractor's claw and its tunnel — a 1911 that fails to eject is usually carrying years of hardened residue in that tunnel, not a broken part.
deepSteps.quote: Using pin punch, pull extractor by groove where firing pin stop runs.
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ This edition prints NO page folios; printed pages below are read off the figure captions that sit on the same page. — PERIODIC CLEANING: EXTRACTOR (printed p.61, per Figure 61-1 on the page)

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent-wet patch, then a bristle brush end to end, then dry patches until clean
Clean the chamber as well as the bore — feeding problems live there

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Bristle brush and solvent on the breech face and around the extractor claw
Wipe the slide rails and the underside of the slide
Light oil on the rails only

cleaning.name: FRAME & FEED RAMP
tasks: Powder residue off every component with solvent on a patch
If the lower is especially dirty, remove the grip panels before soaking or flushing, and get all of it out afterwards

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wipe the body, follower and lips; check the lips are undamaged
No oil inside a magazine — it collects grit and reaches the ammunition

reassembly: Barrel into the front of the slide, link tilted forward.
Barrel bushing in through the front and rotated back to the right.
Recoil spring and guide in through the rear of the slide — the guide and spring must line up with the barrel before the slide goes on.
Slide onto the frame rails and run back until the disassembly notch meets the slide stop hole.
Slide stop in from the left — its shaft MUST pass through the hole in the barrel link, which means the link has to be flipped forward first.
Recoil spring plug over the spring, thumb on the plug, bushing rotated counterclockwise over it — muzzle away from your face.
Two-piece guide rod (if fitted): front section back in and tightened with the 5/32 Allen wrench.
fncheck: Reassemble, then prove it: magazine out, chamber empty, muzzle safe. Rack the slide by hand several times and feel it run without binding on the bushing. Check the thumb safety engages only with the hammer cocked and blocks the trigger; check the grip safety releases the trigger only when the web of your hand depresses it. An improperly assembled 1911 is dangerous — if anything feels wrong, stop and see a gunsmith rather than shooting it.
